data.narrative:
Tevel Aerobotics is a Series B-stage drone and autonomous systems company that has raised $42.6M to date. The broader Drones & Autonomous sector includes eight identifiable private peers (Elroy Air, Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation among them), though no public comparables exist. The peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage clustering to support multiples-based valuation.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised ($43M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement yields an implied valuation of $81M. This reflects the expected value creation between Series B and the subsequent financing round, absent transaction evidence or detailed operating metrics.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $69M (low) to $93M (high), with a median point of $81M. This range rests on a single methodological leg; key uncertainties include the actual revenue run-rate and customer concentration (not provided), the timing and terms of next-round fundraising, and whether stage-progression multiples from the broader venture universe properly calibrate to frontier aerospace/autonomy subsector dynamics. Peer multiples remain inaccessible given the sparse same-stage comparable universe. Updated operating and customer data would materially sharpen this estimate.
